text:
nora: Heads-up — Customer X (enterprise/legal-sensitive) wants us to pin model 'gpt-open-3-large' for 6 months while they finish validation. They asked for: explicit onboarding acceptance metrics, a canary rollout plan, and a documented rollback path. Need product + eng + ML alignment by EOD.

mike: Quick Q — are they asking for a hard pin (no auto-roll) or a pinned traffic route with fallback? that changes infra work.

nora: They want a hard pin for their routes (no auto-upgrade). But they're open to a canary for new customers. We should treat it as a pin request first.

anya: From ML side: we need to know which eval sets they care about. For acceptance I'd ask for: generation quality on their 3 benchmark suites, embedding drift <= 2% L2 on their vectors, and no more than 5% increase in hallucination rate measured via our error taxonomy.

ryan: Also include perf targets — they mentioned tight SLAs. Suggest: P95 latency <= 250ms on dedicated capacity, and error rate <0.5% per 1000 requests.

katie: Customer success says they will only accept if we provide a comms window for deprecation and a migration runway. 6 months pin OK but we need explicit end-of-life triggers and migration incentives.

mike: Operational concerns: hard pin requires us to support the older model binary for the pinned tenant in Dedicated and Private. That adds storage + patching surface. We need an estimate of cost delta from finance before committing.

sam: Platform follow-up: we can implement a per-tenant model routing rule. Work items:
- config flag on routes to bind model version
- alerting if that model is sunset in registry
- fallback policy if capacity exhausted

sam: I'll sketch the canary + fallback policy as RFC after this thread.

anya: Proposed acceptance checklist (draft):
```
- Benchmarks (customer datasets): pass >= 90% of golden QA items (precision/recall thresholds defined per dataset)
- Embedding similarity drift: <= 2% L2 change versus baseline
- Hallucination rate: <= 5% (taxonomy-based)
- Response latency: P95 <= 250ms on dedicated nodes
- Token-level cost: within 15% of current model cost to avoid billing surprises
``` 

nora: This is great. Product asks: can we give the customer a single-page exportable acceptance spec (so their auditors can sign off)? Also need rollback triggers spelled out.

mike: Rollback triggers I'd propose:
- any latency regression > 30% sustained over 15m
- production accuracy drop > 8% on their monitor set
- availability < 99% in a 6h window
On trigger: automatic traffic shift to fallback model and ops page alerted.

ryan: For canary: 1% traffic for 24h, 10% for 48h, then 50% for a week before full. For pinned tenants we skip auto canary unless they opt in.

katie: Sales note: if we push too hard on cost recovery, customer may resist pin. Recommend offering a small discount on pinned capacity and a migration assistance credit.

nora: Action items: everyone add final acceptance thresholds + implementation notes. I'll consolidate into a one-pager and send to Customer X tomorrow. Please add comments inline here.

mike: I'll add infra cost estimate by EOD.

anya: I'll convert the checklist into our eval harness tests and add a runbook for hallucination labeling.

sam: RFC for routing + fallback by tomorrow morning.

ryan: I'll draft the canary schedule and monitoring dashboard queries.

katie: I'll prepare the customer comms draft + discount proposal.

deploy-bot: Note: past 30 days there have been 2 pinned-model requests in backlog; existing SLA docs updated at 2649000000.

nora: Thanks — tagging @everyone implicitly. If no objections, I'll pin this thread as the canonical spec for the ask.
